title: Land in the same step when checks turn green during the poll
summary: Make the drain's locked rebase, re-check and land step merge a pull request as soon as its checks go green during the poll, rather than returning Landing::Waiting and retrying about 10 minutes later. Still-pending checks at the end of the poll keep today's Waiting behaviour. The audience is the person running the drain, who loses about 10 minutes per job.

defaults_applied.how: Two new tests, with cargo test and clippy clean.
Criteria check that the job lands or waits, by running the tests.
The check is that the job merges in the same step when the checks go green.
The producer must locate where Waiting is returned despite a green poll.
All code and tests are Rust.
Comments are written for an outside reader.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: I read crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs. Drain::land takes the landing lock, runs recheck_after_rebase, then calls Steps::land and maps Landing::Landed, NotLanded or Waiting to a LandStep. PrLander::land calls athena.land_pr with crate::wiring::checks_poll, and landing_from_report maps an open pull request with Checks::Pending to Landing::Waiting. I also read crates/athena-core/src/gh/landing.rs (land_pr) and crates/athena-core/src/gh/early.rs (wait_for_checks). wait_for_checks already stops polling at the first non-pending read, and land_pr merges when the result is Green and merge_via_rest is on. So the stated bug may be in drain.rs or wiring.rs, or already fixed in core; the producer must find where Waiting is returned despite a green poll and reproduce it first.

The drain.rs test World/Steps fake has a `waiting` set that makes land return Waiting; the new tests extend that fake or call landing_from_report and Drain::land directly. The tests drive a scripted checks sequence (pending then green) with a counting fake and no real sleep.
No new record or data file under crates/ is added, so the records validation allow-list (check_record_file, AnyRecord) is not touched.

The fix is confined to crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs and its tests as the request says. A minimal change to crates/athena-cli/src/wiring.rs or crates/athena-core/src/gh is allowed only if the root cause is there, and then it is a listed deliverable.
Merging only on green is preserved: a Red or still-Pending result never reaches the merge. This is not a new refusal rule, so no refusal-rate criterion applies.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new test in crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs scripts checks that are pending at first and green partway through the poll. It shows the job reports Landing::Landed (the job line is 'landed') in the same land step, with no Landing::Waiting returned and no second land call. Check with `cargo test -p athena-cli drain`.

A new test scripts checks that are still pending when the poll ends. It shows the result is still Landing::Waiting, the job line still starts 'waiting to merge', and the item is not retried. This is today's behaviour. Check with `cargo test -p athena-cli drain`.

The existing tests a_job_waiting_to_merge_is_not_a_failure_and_the_run_goes_on_to_the_next_job and a_merge_refused_for_rule_violations_while_checks_are_pending_is_reported_as_waiting still pass unchanged. Red checks still give NotLanded. Check with `cargo test -p athena-cli`.
`cargo test` passes for the workspace, `cargo clippy --all-targets` is clean and `cargo fmt --check` passes.

The diff touches only crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs, plus any file where the root cause is found. Comments or docs near the Landing::Waiting handling say that a poll which turns green merges in the same step.

Outcome check: the diff shows the green-during-poll path ending in a merge in one locked step, rather than only adding types or wiring. Each new test would fail on the old code for the green-during-poll case.

out_of_scope: Changing the poll length or interval
Changing the merge gate: merge only when every check is green and merge_via_rest is on
Changing the rebase and re-check rule
departures: The poll code in athena-core already seems to merge on green, so the root cause is uncertain. That adds some risk to the verification pass rate and a little to the cost.
urgent_reason: It cuts about 10 minutes per job of waiting and retrying, which is wasted time in the drain.
hard_reason: It changes the drain's landing step (the locked rebase, re-check and merge pipeline), where a mistake could merge a pull request whose checks are not green.
